Source The actor reflects on his childhood connection with Charles Dickens’ classic and bringing the iconic Ebenezer Scrooge to life in Paramount Pictures’ haunting reimagining, arriving in Indian cinemas on 20th November.
 Giving Christmas a dark, twisted spin this November is Johnny Depp, who steps into the iconic role of Ebenezer Scrooge in a haunting reimagining of Charles Dickens’ timeless classic, Paramount Pictures’ Ebenezer. Known for his transformative portrayals of complex characters and misfits, Depp explores the pain and past behind Scrooge’s cold exterior.
 Reflecting on his long-standing familiarity with A Christmas Carol and what drew him to the role, Depp said in an interview during the recent UK promotions, “I've been familiar with A Christmas Carol since I've been a very little kid. I used to watch the Alastair Sim’s version. Every Christmas, I would look forward to watching that film. And I've watched it on loops, you know, over the years, without ever having the intention or the idea of me playing Scrooge.
 When I got the offer to play Ebenezer Scrooge, my first reaction was - I just smiled. Because even though Alastair Sim, I believe, is the ultimate Scrooge, and a lot of people have played Scrooge, Sim’s was perfect. So that, in itself, for me was the challenge. The challenge to find a different way into Ebenezer Scrooge. So is he just simply a mean, old, miserly guy?
 It takes something to get there, you know. So I felt that Ebenezer's basic, ultimate life dilemma was that, at a certain point, he had to stop himself from caring because it hurt him too much. So he then just went inward.”
 Looking beyond Scrooge’s familiar image as a miserly and bitter old man, Depp sees him as a deeply wounded individual, shaped by difficult experiences and his upbringing. Describing his interpretation of the character, he said, “The character is more tragic than hateful, more a product of certain experiences and his upbringing. A broken human being.”
 At its heart, Ebenezer explores themes of redemption, self-reflection and the possibility of transformation. Speaking about the emotional journey at the centre of the story and how revisiting one's past can offer a path towards change, Depp added, “With the opportunity to go back inside, travel through his life and see it from a different angle to understand how he became what he became, and that some people can be brought back, you know, from that deep abyss of just self-hatred and yeah, total antisocial behavior. It's a very beautiful story, but it's certainly a story of life experience and eventuality.”
 Joining Johnny Depp in this haunting adventure are Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Robert Strange, Tramell Tillman, and Ian McKellen, who play pivotal roles in this fresh take on Charles Dickens’ beloved ghost story.
 Ebenezer, based on Charles Dickens’ beloved novella A Christmas Carol, is directed by Ti West and screenplay by Nathaniel Halpern,. It is executive produced by Ti West, Adam Bohling, David Reid, Stephen Deuters, Jason Forman, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Molly Smith, Thad Luckinbill, Trent Luckinbill and produced by Emma Watts.
 Produced by Paramount Pictures, Ebenezer releases in cinemas across India on 20th November 2026.
